# Plan permissions and API prechecks

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

Choose a permission check for the protected resource and treat the result as advisory evidence before the server authorizes a request.

[Documentation home](../INDEX.md)

Choose the check that corresponds to the resource you will access:

| Question | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Does the user have a permission in the current SharePoint context? | [useSPFxPermissions](../api/hooks/permissions.md#usespfxpermissions) |
| What permissions apply on another web? | [useSPFxCrossSitePermissions](../api/hooks/permissions.md#usespfxcrosssitepermissions) |
| Is the configured delegated Graph/custom API scope present in an acquired token? | [useSPFxApiPermissionPrecheck](../api/hooks/http-clients/api-permission-precheck.md) |
| How can this run outside React? | [Permission helpers](../api/helpers/permission.md), [precheck helpers](../api/helpers/api-permission-precheck.md), [precheck service](../api/services/api-permission-precheck.md) |

A token scope precheck diagnoses configuration and consent; it does not prove that a particular server resource will authorize the request. SharePoint masks, Graph delegated scopes and destination-list grants answer different questions. Handle pending, failed and denied checks separately, then handle actual request failures as documented by the selected client or service.

Follow the precheck reference for remediation entries in `webApiPermissionRequests`, token acquisition behavior, configuration states and retry options. Any required tenant approval remains an explicit administrator operation. See the [authenticated Graph/storage checklist](../development/sharepoint-validation/INDEX.md#permissions-denial-and-absence) for real account and permission evidence.

## Scoped checks and conditional rendering

Use the [scoped permission overload](../api/hooks/permissions.md) for a specific web, list, item or folder. Supply the scope's documented selector; URL/list identity and errors remain distinct from a negative permission result. The legacy staged-URL overload retains its separate execution contract.

[SharePointPermissionTrim](../api/controls/sharepoint-permission-trim.md), [SharePointGroupTrim](../api/controls/sharepoint-group-trim.md) and [EntraGroupTrim](../api/controls/entra-group-trim.md) compose render branches around the current decision. Keep loading, denied and failed states distinguishable. Entra membership checks require the documented existing delegated grants and can be limited by hidden membership or incomplete directory information. Conditional rendering is not server authorization.

#### Check real delegated token diagnostics

```ts
import type { SPFxAadTokenProviderLike } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

import { createSPFxApiPermissionPrecheckService } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
async function demonstrate(tokenProvider: SPFxAadTokenProviderLike) {
  const diagnostics = createSPFxApiPermissionPrecheckService(tokenProvider);
  const results = await diagnostics.check({
    graph: ['User.Read', { scope: 'Mail.Read', required: false }],
  }, { useCachedToken: false, timeoutMs: 10000 });
  for (const result of results) console.log(result.scope, result.status, result.packageSolutionEntry);
}
```

#### Compare illustrative Graph and Orders API requirements

```ts
import {
  evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement,
  normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements,
  summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults,
  SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID,
  type SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckConfig,
  type SPFxJwtPayload,
} from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const config: SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckConfig = {
  graph: [
    'Sites.Read.All',
    { scope: 'User.Read', required: false, label: 'Profile access' },
  ],
  customApis: [{
    id: 'orders',
    name: 'Orders API',
    resource: 'api://11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111',
    packageResource: 'Orders API',
    scopes: [{ scope: 'Orders.Read', satisfies: ['Orders.ReadWrite'] }],
    expectedAudiences: ['11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111'],
  }],
};

const requirements = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements(config);
// Illustrative decoded claims only; use the hook/service for real tokens.
const graphPayload: SPFxJwtPayload = {
  aud: SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID,
  scp: 'Sites.Read.All User.Read',
};
const graphResults = requirements
  .filter(requirement => requirement.id.startsWith('graph:'))
  .map(requirement =>
    evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement(requirement, graphPayload)
  );
const graphSummary = summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults(graphResults);
// Both Graph requirements are available: configurationState === 'ready'.
// Custom API requirements need their own resource token and are not checked here.
```

## Snapshot checks and server authorization

Pass a host `SPPermission` set and the requested SharePoint permission bit. This synchronous capability check performs no I/O, requires no provider and does not acquire Graph/API scopes. An available permission flag is an indication from the supplied snapshot; SharePoint still authorizes actual requests. The helper does not catch failures from a supplied object's `hasPermission` implementation.

## Effective resource permissions

### useSPFxCrossSitePermissions

The legacy string overload remains supported. Undefined, empty or whitespace-only `siteUrl` returns idle state without fetching; `hasSitePermission`, `hasWebPermission` and `hasListPermission` then return false. With a URL it retrieves site-collection root-web permissions, selected-web permissions and optionally list permissions. `options.webUrl` defaults to `siteUrl`; `listId` is a hyphenated GUID with optional paired braces. The result names and optional permission sets are unchanged.

The site set uses `/_api/site/rootweb/effectivebasepermissions`. This endpoint follows the documented [SP.Site.rootWeb resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/office/sharepoint-visio/jj245543(v=office.15)) to [SP.Web.EffectiveBasePermissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/office/sharepoint-visio/jj245395(v=office.15)); the former `/_api/site/effectivebasepermissions` request addressed a property absent from SP.Site. Site permissions therefore describe the collection's root web, including when the URL points to a subweb.

Provider, native client, current user and target changes hide previous sets during render, before effects start their replacement request. Obsolete and unmounted completions cannot publish results. HTTP failures and malformed permission masks expose `error` and no grant. Server authorization still applies.

Pass an options object to select one resource:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { SPFxScopedPermissionsOptions, useSPFxCrossSitePermissions } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
function SelectedItem() {
  const target: SPFxScopedPermissionsOptions = {
    scope: 'item', listTitle: 'Tasks', itemId: 42,
  };
  const permission = useSPFxCrossSitePermissions(target);
  return <span>{permission.isLoading ? 'Loading' : 'Ready'}</span>;
}
```

`SPFxScopedPermissionsOptions` is a discriminated union. The full [SPFxScopedPermissionsOptions](../api/hooks/permissions.md#spfxscopedpermissionsoptions) reference documents its valid shapes, required/disallowed branch inputs and optional `webUrl`.

`webUrl` defaults to the current provider web and must be absolute HTTP(S) without credentials, query or fragment. `listId` is a hyphenated GUID, optionally in paired braces. `listTitle` matches the exact nonblank title, including apostrophes/spaces. `listPath` is a **decoded web-relative list root** such as `Shared Documents` or `Lists/Tasks`, without a leading slash. `folderPath` is **decoded server-relative**, such as `/sites/team/Shared Documents/Reports`. Supply literal spaces, percent signs and hash characters; do not URL-encode input. Paths reject schemes, backslashes, queries and dot segments. `itemId` is valid only for item scope, and `folderPath` only for folder scope. Runtime validation also rejects invalid JavaScript callers before any HTTP dispatch.

For current-web scope, an available mask is read through `useSPFxPermissions` without REST. If it is unavailable, or the target web differs, the hook uses the native SPHttpClient. List and item scope request their own effective mask, without requesting unrelated site/web masks. Folder scope reads selected-list identity and the folder's list item with its permission mask and parent-list identity; a mismatching or missing parent list is an error. It does not infer folder permissions from the list or a path prefix. A library's root folder may lack a list item; use list scope for that resource.

`permissions` is undefined during loading, validation/HTTP/payload errors and target replacement. `hasPermission` returns false when the mask is unavailable and otherwise requires every bit in the supplied native `SPPermission`. `isLoading` is false for native-mask success and validation errors. `error` holds only the current failure. A newly allocated object with equivalent scalar values does not repeat requests. Concurrent identical requests may share an inflight promise **only within one provider and matching client/user identity**; completed decisions are not cached and there is no polling or refresh timer. Changing provider, client, user or target immediately discards old asynchronous decisions. In-place host changes still require a React render; the hook does not subscribe independently to every PageContext field.

Requires a matching SPFx provider and its native PageContext/SPHttpClient; it imports no PnP feature registrations. Local behavior/type tests use native boundary doubles and do not establish authenticated SharePoint results. The Context demo includes a staged scoped target and explicit Run/repeat, alongside the unchanged legacy staged URL view. The [SharePointPermissionTrim](../api/controls/sharepoint-permission-trim.md) sample composes this same hook; [authenticated scoped checks](../development/sharepoint-validation/INDEX.md) remain separate. A permission check is a UI decision; SharePoint remains responsible for authorization.

## Passive delegated checks

### `SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckMode`

`'passive' | 'interactiveAllowed'` configures the [precheck hook](../api/hooks/http-clients/api-permission-precheck.md). Its default is `passive`, which registers cancellation handlers for authentication popup/redirect events when supported by the token provider. `interactiveAllowed` permits the provider's normal authentication behavior. The standalone helpers do not acquire tokens or enforce an interaction mode; the [precheck service](../api/services/api-permission-precheck.md) accepts a token provider supplied by its caller.

## Diagnostics and real resource tokens

`decodeSPFxJwtPayload` parses a JWT payload and returns `undefined` for a decoding failure or a non-object payload. It does not verify signatures or validate the claim schema. Evaluation checks supplied expiry/not-before claims and, by default, configured audiences, but this remains diagnostic-only token interpretation. An `available` result is not proof that the target API will authorize a request, and the helpers must not serve as a security boundary. Acquire real tokens through the [hook](../api/hooks/http-clients/api-permission-precheck.md) or [service](../api/services/api-permission-precheck.md) and let the API enforce authorization.

## Permissions by enabled file feature

### Permissions by enabled feature

The baseline obtains a SharePoint-audience token through AadTokenProvider. SPHttpClient metadata access and iframe bearer-token authorization are distinct; success of one does not prove the other's grants. Permissions are delegated and bounded by user rights; existing shared SPFx tenant grants may already suffice.

| Feature | SharePoint delegated permission | Optional Graph dependency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SharePoint read selection | MyFiles.Read or AllSites.Read | None required by baseline |
| Current-user OneDrive read | MyFiles.Read | None required by baseline |
| SharePoint native upload/create | MyFiles.Write or AllSites.Write | No inherent Graph requirement |
| OneDrive native upload/create | MyFiles.Write | No inherent Graph requirement |
| Teams-channel discovery when requested by service | AllSites.Read; AllSites.Write for write | ChannelSettings.Read.All |
| Presentation/filter/selection settings | No extra grant solely for configuration | None |
| Claims challenge | Same approved resource and extra claims | Does not itself grant any new permission |

Microsoft also lists Graph Files.Read/Files.ReadWrite alternatives in its operation table; these do not substitute a Graph token for the SharePoint-audience token used by our hosted iframe. Do not union all scopes from the sample. Optional service pivots may request additional audiences; test the actual enabled experience before declaring a minimal deployment. The toolkit changes neither the package manifest nor tenant approvals. The consumer configuration below requests the baseline only when that grant is not already approved.

### SharePoint-audience baseline request

Add this request to the consuming SPFx application's `package-solution.json` only when an existing approved SharePoint grant does not already cover the feature:

```json
{ "webApiPermissionRequests": [{ "resource": "SharePoint", "scope": "MyFiles.Read" }] }
```

For a consumer choosing an all-sites read grant use AllSites.Read instead; add write or Graph requests separately only for enabled capabilities. Admin approval and user rights are still required. See [Microsoft permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/developer/controls/file-pickers/?view=odsp-graph-online) and [SPFx API access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/dev/spfx/use-aadhttpclient).

## Entra content trimming

`EntraGroupTrim` is a headless current-user access trim. Import the compound value and its types from the package root or controls barrel. It requires a matching SPFx provider; place it within the provider appropriate for your actual host.

### Directory contract

Requires a matching SPFx provider with its native MSGraphClientV3 factory. All-ID member checks do not resolve group existence: an unreturned GUID is denied and cannot distinguish a missing group from nonmembership. All-ID member checks use `/me/checkMemberGroups` with deduplicated chunks of at most twenty and avoid metadata reads. Graph membership is transitive for security groups; Microsoft 365 group membership is direct. Names query escaped exact displayName, inspect all pages, apply the requested groupType **locally before ambiguity**, and fail on missing/ambiguous matches. A specific typed ID requires metadata; a mismatch is an error, not a denied check. No advanced query headers/eventual-index assumptions are added.

Owners read `/me` and every direct owners page; ID-only limited-information objects suffice. Metadata-confirmed synchronized groups, distribution groups and non-Unified mail-enabled groups have unsupported ownership and select ErrorFallback before member/owner reads, including memberOrOwner. Every requested read must succeed; `any` or a positive member result cannot hide another read failure. HTTP/Graph/payload errors never become partial grants. Hidden membership may be omitted by Graph: absence in a response is not proof of real-world absence.

The sample solution config requests Microsoft Graph `User.Read` and `GroupMember.Read.All`; deployment and tenant approval are separate and have not been performed. Graph consent/access and additional permissions required for hidden membership or constrained groups must be checked in the actual tenant. A configured permission request is not proof of an approved grant. See the [HTTP client guide](http-clients.md) and [host checklist](../development/sharepoint-validation/INDEX.md).

### Structural branches and lifetime

Place `Loading`, `Fallback` and `ErrorFallback` once each as **direct** children of their own family. They are structural content markers, not Fluent slots. The trim emits caller content without a DOM wrapper. Loading means a current read is pending; Fallback means all requested reads succeeded and access did not match; ErrorFallback means validation, transport, payload or resolution failed. Errors never select Fallback. Every omitted branch renders empty, including an omitted ErrorFallback. An absent `children` prop renders empty.

Inactive protected/branch components never render, run effects or mount. Caller DOM, class names, refs and formatting belong on the caller's children. Controls and markers expose no public DOM, class/style/ref or callback props. Changing the active role or the structural marker's React key remounts its content; the same role/key preserves caller state and child keys. Child arrays/keys remain meaningful. React 17's broad `ReactNode` type can admit functions through its historical `{}` alternative; callbacks are unsupported and never executed.

Duplicate, wrong-family and detectable fragment-wrapped markers fail closed. Keep markers direct rather than hiding them inside wrappers/fragments or custom components. Markers are supported only as direct children of their own trim family. A standalone marker renders its children unconditionally and performs no access check; standalone usage is unsupported. Custom components are ordinary protected children, not a way to declare a structural branch.

Provider, native client, PageContext/current-user identity and target changes hide previous asynchronous grants during render. Obsolete/unmounted requests cannot restore them. Identical inflight reads may be shared within the matching provider only; settled grants are not cached and there is no polling. Host changes still require a React render. Run/repeat in the sample deliberately changes the trim key to perform a fresh check. UI trimming is advisory; each server operation still needs authorization.

The lazy **Entra Group Trim** sample uses this actual control and native APIs, editable selectors, enum fields, all three branches, a protected counter and effect mount gauge. Local fixtures replace only unavailable transports and do not establish authenticated tenant behavior. See [development verification](../development/INDEX.md) and the [controls index](../api/INDEX.md#references).

`EntraGroupTrimBranchProps` describes each structural marker. `EntraGroupTrimProps` describes the control.

Graph paging currently accepts HTTPS next links on `graph.microsoft.com` only. National-cloud or other next-link hosts select ErrorFallback; those endpoints are not supported by this adapter.

## SharePoint group trimming

`SharePointGroupTrim` is a headless current-user access trim. Import the compound value and its types from the package root or controls barrel. It requires a matching SPFx provider; place it within the provider appropriate for your actual host.

### Direct membership contract

Requires a matching SPFx provider and native SPHttpClient. Reads the selected web's current-user site-local ID and direct users for every selected site group across all pages. This does not expand Entra principals nested in SharePoint groups and does not query a transitive directory membership. Exact names use escaped Title filters, local exact equality and all-page ambiguity checks. Missing or ambiguous groups, invalid IDs, HTTP/payload/paging failures are errors; an earlier positive membership cannot hide a later failure. Remote-web IDs belong to that web's site collection.

The lazy **SharePoint Group Trim** sample uses this actual control and native APIs, editable selectors, enum fields, all three branches, a protected counter and effect mount gauge. Local fixtures replace only unavailable transports and do not establish authenticated tenant behavior. See [development verification](../development/INDEX.md) and the [controls index](../api/INDEX.md#references).

`SharePointGroupTrimBranchProps` describes each structural marker. `SharePointGroupTrimProps` describes the control.

## Resource-specific content trimming

`SharePointPermissionTrim` is a headless current-user access trim. Import the compound value and its types from the package root or controls barrel. It requires a matching SPFx provider; place it within the provider appropriate for your actual host.

### Resource contract

`SharePointPermissionTrimProps` inherits `SPFxScopedPermissionsOptions`. `SharePointPermissionTrimProps.scope` defaults to `web`, and `SharePointPermissionTrimProps.webUrl` defaults to the provider's current web. URLs must be absolute HTTP(S), without credentials/query/fragment. `SharePointPermissionTrimProps.listId`, `SharePointPermissionTrimProps.listTitle` and `SharePointPermissionTrimProps.listPath` are mutually exclusive; exactly one is required for list/item/folder and forbidden for web. IDs are GUIDs with optional paired braces; titles match exact nonblank text; listPath is decoded web-relative root without a leading slash, query, backslash or dot segments. `SharePointPermissionTrimProps.itemId` is a positive integer required only for item; `SharePointPermissionTrimProps.folderPath` is a decoded server-relative folder path required only for folder. A folder must resolve to a list item belonging to the selected list. Use list scope for a library root folder without a list item.

Available current-web masks use `useSPFxPermissions` without REST and inherit PageContext freshness. A missing mask or remote web uses native SPHttpClient. Scoped resources read their own effective permissions, not unrelated masks. HTTP/payload failures produce ErrorFallback with no partial grants. Requires a matching SPFx provider and its native PageContext/SPHttpClient; no PnP registrations are required.

The lazy **SharePoint Permission Trim** sample uses this actual control and native APIs, editable selectors, enum fields, all three branches, a protected counter and effect mount gauge. Local fixtures replace only unavailable transports and do not establish authenticated tenant behavior. See [development verification](../development/INDEX.md) and the [controls index](../api/INDEX.md#references).

### AND composition

Nest actual trims to require both decisions. The inner check mounts only when the outer check allows, so an outer denial/error does not start the inner request. The Permission Trim sample includes this selectable composition. Its nested Entra check additionally needs the native Graph client and approved User.Read/GroupMember.Read.All access.

`SharePointPermissionTrimBranchProps` describes each structural marker. `SharePointPermissionTrimProps` describes the control.

#### Compare a gate and manual passive recheck

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { useSPFxApiPermissionPrecheck } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
function OrdersPermissionGate({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const precheck = useSPFxApiPermissionPrecheck({ graph: ['Sites.Read.All'], customApis: [{
    name: 'Orders API', resource: 'api://contoso-orders-api', packageResource: 'Orders API', scopes: ['Orders.Read'],
  }] });
  return precheck.configurationState === 'ready' ? <>{children}</> : <section>
    <p>{precheck.isChecking ? 'Checking API access' : precheck.configurationState}</p>
    {precheck.missing.map(item => <p key={item.id}>{item.adminMessage}</p>)}
  </section>;
}
function ManualPermissionCheck() {
  const precheck = useSPFxApiPermissionPrecheck({ graph: ['Sites.Read.All'] }, { autoCheck: false, mode: 'passive' });
  return <div><button disabled={precheck.isChecking} onClick={() => void precheck.check().catch(console.error)}>Check now</button>
    <button disabled={precheck.isChecking} onClick={() => void precheck.retryWithoutCache().catch(console.error)}>Recheck without cache</button>
    <pre>{precheck.configurationState}</pre>
  </div>;
}
```
